hero.title: Dentistry in Italy – The Complete Guide for International Students
hero.subtitle: Pursue a 6-year, 360 ECTS single-cycle degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics (Odontoiatria e Protesi Dentaria) combining medical sciences, simulation labs, and supervised clinical training.

overview: Dentistry in Italy is an option for students interested in oral healthcare, dental science, clinical training and professional development in Europe. The six-year single-cycle degree in Dental Medicine and Dental Prosthodontics offered by Italian universities is based on the integration of scientific foundations and practical and clinical education. The common name for the qualification in Italy is Odontoiatria e Protesi Dentaria.

Students who wish to Study Dentistry in Italy should check the language of instruction, admission rules, tuition fees, clinical training and professional registration requirements before selecting a university. The majority of dentistry courses are delivered in Italian, so students should check if an officially English-taught option is available for their intended intake.

With support from Edu-Hawk Worldwide, students can check out suitable universities, know admission procedures, organize academic documents and plan their applications per official university requirements.

items: Italy is a desirable destination for Indian students looking for quality dental education, advanced clinical facilities and international exposure. Italian universities have organized dental programs combining theoretical knowledge, laboratory training and practical clinical experience.
Top benefits of studying dentistry in Italy:
International Education: Italian universities meet European standards for higher education and offer a structured dental education.
English-taught Programs: International students can find dentistry programs taught in English at several universities.
Affordable Education: Depending on the university and student's eligibility, public universities may have comparatively affordable tuition fees.
Advanced Clinical Facilities: Students are exposed to dental laboratories, modern equipment and healthcare technologies.
Practical Training: The program includes laboratory work, simulation training and supervised clinical experience.
European Exposure: Students get to experience international academic culture and meet students from different countries.
Specialization Opportunities: Graduates can advance their education in orthodontics, oral surgery, prosthodontics and other dental fields.
Students studying Dentistry in Italy can combine academic education with international exposure and prepare for a professional career in oral healthcare.
In Italy, Dentistry Courses are delivered via an integrated university degree program called Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics (Odontoiatria e Protesi Dentaria).
The program normally lasts six years and involves 360 ECTS credits. Students learn basic medical sciences, dental sciences, laboratory techniques and clinical dentistry.
The curriculum progresses from basic medical sciences to specialized dental subjects and supervised clinical training.

items: Indian students looking to study Dentistry in Italy must fulfill the academic, language, and admission criteria of the university they want to join.
Compulsory subjects: Physics, Chemistry and Biology.
Minimum academic marks set by the university.
NEET qualification wherever required under Indian regulations for studying dentistry abroad.

sections.title: Cost of Dentistry Studies in Italy

items: Italy has a wide range of study options for international students. The total cost depends on the university, city, accommodation, lifestyle and program.
The following estimates are given in Indian Rupees. Estimated conversion: €1 = ₹100 (indicative, not a fixed exchange rate).
University fees at public universities may be subject to university regulations, income assessment, fee categories and applicable concessions.
For example, the University of Siena's published tuition fee estimate for its English-taught dentistry program is around €4,496 per year, or roughly ₹4.50 lakh.
UniCamillus has published its tuition fees for its Italian-language program in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics at €16,000 per year (roughly ₹16 lakh per year excluding additional expenses).
Living costs vary depending on the city, the type of accommodation and personal lifestyle.

These estimates do not include travel, visa charges, insurance, dental instruments, clinical materials and other additional expenses. Actual costs will vary depending on the university and city you choose.

items: In Italy, students graduating in Dentistry have to meet the relevant professional requirements before being allowed to work as dentists.
To be eligible for work as a dentist in Italy, graduates need to meet the necessary requirements for qualification, licensing and professional registration, such as:
Completion of the approved Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics course.
Meeting any relevant professional qualification requirements.
Going through the necessary procedure of professional registration.
Registration with the competent Italian professional body.
Meeting Italian language and patient communication needs.
Adhering to professional standards and healthcare regulations.
Practising in India After Dentistry in Italy
Indian students desirous of returning to India must fulfill applicable dental regulatory and licensing requirements. Students should check before enrolling:
Recognition requirements for the chosen university and program.
Course length, clinical training and qualification criteria.
Relevant exams and registration requirements for the profession.
Eligibility for registration and to practice dentistry in India.
Having a dentistry degree from abroad does not equate to automatic permission to practice in India.

Dentistry provides career opportunities in hospitals, dental clinics, private practice, healthcare organizations and academic institutions. After obtaining the required qualification and professional registration, graduates can seek employment opportunities in Italy or abroad, subject to local licensing regulations.
Specialized positions usually require additional post-graduate education, training or professional qualifications.
These are illustrative, broad estimates and not guaranteed salary offers. Actual earnings are based on experience, professional registration, employment type, city and specialization.
Independent dentists may earn different amounts than those who work for a salary, because their income is dependent on the number of patients, operating costs and business expenses.

faq.question: How many years does it take to finish Dentistry in Italy?
faq.answer: The study of dentistry and dental prosthodontics takes 6 years (360 ECTS credits) and includes theoretical education, practical training and clinical experience.

faq.question: Can Indian students study Dentistry in Italy in English?
faq.answer: Yes. Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics programs in English are offered by selected Italian universities. Students should check the up-to-date course language, eligibility requirements and availability of seats for international applicants.

faq.question: How much does it cost to study Dentistry in Italy in INR?
faq.answer: The total estimated cost of a six-year program, including tuition fees and living expenses, could be between about ₹55.80 lakh and ₹1.03 crore. The real cost will depend on the university, the city, the accommodation and your personal lifestyle.

faq.question: Is NEET compulsory for Indian students to study Dentistry in Italy?
faq.answer: Where required under applicable Indian regulations for pursuing dentistry abroad, Indian students should qualify NEET. They must also meet the requirements for admission to an Italian university.

faq.question: After completing Dentistry in Italy, can I practice in India?
faq.answer: Students can pursue dental practice in India after meeting the relevant Indian qualification recognition, licensing, registration and professional requirements. Before enrolling, they should verify the current regulations with the appropriate Indian authorities.
